topics.topic: Deterministic validation and publication order for function and trial outputs
questions: In what order are multiple output ports and their target edges checked, and are all checks completed before any StoredValue or SpooledFile is published, so that different implementations cannot leave different unnamed bytes or hit different spool ceilings?
In what order are multiple output ports and many-file elements validated, stored or spooled, and which failure wins if more than one output violates a post-sandbox value or spool ceiling?

quotes: execute_function: [RETURN_SHAPE] Returns SandboxResult with the outcome, outputs only for succeeded as PortPayload entries in output port name order (a value as its canonical JSON bytes, a file as its bytes, a many file port as the list of its bytes), resources_used with elapsed wall_time_ms, peak memory_bytes and the output count as output_bytes, failure_detail, and detail_code None except for cleanup_failed.

execute_trial_case: [BEHAVIOR] The outcome is the sandbox outcome of the same name; a succeeded execution is passed when the case has no expected outputs or every output's digest equals the expected one, a many file output equal only with the same length and equal digests position by position, and output_mismatch otherwise; a succeeded value output whose canonical bytes exceed the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant makes the outcome contract_violation.

execute_trial_case: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] For passed and output_mismatch the outputs are recorded, a value as a StoredValue stored with put_value_bytes and a file by digest, size and media type only as a FileFactsRef whose disclosure_class is the highest class of the case's inputs, every output taking that class; other outcomes record outputs None; one RecordTrialExecutionChange is written through record_change with resources_used, the sandbox's detail_code (value_too_large for an output over the stored value ceiling), the sandbox's failure_detail, executed_at from kernel_now and the given actor.

execute_function_element: [BEHAVIOR] On an outcome other than succeeded the NodeExecutionDraft carries that outcome as status with the SandboxResult detail_code, failure_detail and resources_used, executed the ExecutedImplementation, the input PortRefs and no outputs. On succeeded, each JSON output above the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant concludes contract_violation with detail value_too_large, the SandboxResult's resources_used and no outputs; otherwise JSON outputs are published with put_value_bytes as StoredValues of the port's stored schema (M21: its value_schema, or for a many port the canonical array schema with it as items), and files are published with spool_file under the run, node, map_index, the element's next attempt_number — the count of its NodeExecutions read with ExecutionsOfElement plus one, the number its record is then written under — the port and the list_index for a many port, a RefusedError from spool_file concluding resource_exhausted with the SandboxResult's resources_used, no outputs and no file of that attempt kept.

spool_file: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise RefusedError when the size of content exceeds the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SPOOL_FILE_BYTES_MAX constant, or when the run's spool, counted as the bytes of the files already in it, less a file no SpooledFile record names at this file's position, plus content, would exceed the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SPOOL_RUN_BYTES_MAX constant; on that refusal it removes this file and every file already spooled under the same run_id, producer_node_id, map_index and attempt_number, so nothing of that attempt's files is kept, while files of earlier attempts stay. The attempt_number of the key is the element's next number as the caller read it; spool_file does not assign one.
judgement.why: State 6 orders sandbox outputs by port name, checks post-sandbox JSON size before publication, preserves many-file list order, and removes every file of the attempt when spooling refuses.

topics.topic: How canonical_bytes retains enough input information to reject duplicate JSON keys
questions: Does canonical_bytes receive raw JSON text with duplicate-member information, or an already-decoded value in which duplicate keys can no longer be detected?
How can this operation observe and reject duplicate object keys if its input is an already-decoded JSON value, which normally cannot retain duplicate keys?

judgement.why: This is the same canonical-bytes duplicate-member question, and the recovery change touched none of its passages.

precedent.topic: Where and how duplicate JSON object members are rejected by canonical_bytes
quotes:
`canonical_bytes` parses JSON text, refuses a duplicate member name,
   a non-finite number and an integer outside ±(2^53 − 1), which an IEEE double
   cannot hold exactly, and emits the JCS form.

canonical_bytes: [BEHAVIOR] MUST parse json_text as one JSON value and emit its RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical form encoded as UTF-8: object members sorted by the UTF-16 code units of their names, numbers written in the ECMAScript shortest round-trip form (an integral double without a fraction or exponent, so a number written 1.0 becomes 1), strings escaped exactly as JCS prescribes, and no whitespace; it applies no Unicode normalization, so two texts that differ only in normalization give different bytes.

canonical_bytes: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise NonCanonicalValueError, with a reason naming the first offending item in text order, when json_text is not one well-formed JSON value, when an object repeats a member name at any depth, when it holds a non-finite number (NaN, Infinity or -Infinity tokens, which the default Python parser would accept and therefore MUST be rejected explicitly), when a number written without a fraction or exponent lies outside plus or minus (2 to the power 53 minus 1), which an IEEE double cannot hold exactly, or when a string holds a lone surrogate.
precedent.why: State 6 makes canonical_bytes consume JSON text and detect repeated member names while parsing it.

topics.topic: Mechanism for reading repository files at a manifest revision
questions: How is a file read at a repository revision: from a checked-out tree that must match the revision, through a version-control lookup, or from a revision-addressed directory/provider?

What operation resolves and reads a path at manifest_revision—an immutable revision-addressed repository read, a checkout prepared by the host, or an ordinary directory read with the revision used only as metadata?

judgement.why: This is the same manifest-revision access question, and the recovery change touched none of its passages.

precedent.topic: Manifest location, revision resolution, and immutable snapshot access
quotes:
**The manifest at a revision**: `manifest_location` is a directory inside a
git repository and `manifest_revision` a commit of it; `bindings` reads
`<service_id>.json` of that directory at that commit as a git object, never
from the working tree, so a record changes only with the configured revision
(A08 rules 1 and 6).
precedent.why: The later contract fixes both revision semantics and immutable access through Git objects rather than the working tree.

precedent.topic: Errors and validation order for missing captured trial-case references
quotes: capture_failed_execution: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST read the NodeExecution of the AttemptKey with RecordsByAttempt, UnknownReferenceError propagating; then raise RefusedError unless its executed is an ExecutedImplementation, its resources_used is present (the function ran in the sandbox; a receiving node that refused a misfit input did not) and its status is not succeeded; then read its Run and raise RefusedError unless the run has not ended, or ended failed with released_by absent.

capture_failed_execution: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST copy nothing itself: after its own checks it calls add_captured_trial_case with the implementation_id of the record's ExecutedImplementation, the named contract version, the record's inputs as they are — a StoredValuesRef as it is and spooled files as their SpooledFilesRef —, the AttemptKey and the actor, and returns its TrialCase; a refusal of add_captured_trial_case propagates as it is and has copied nothing.

add_captured_trial_case: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST first read the Implementation of executed_implementation_id from its own records, UnknownReferenceError propagating; then raises RefusedError naming the first failing check: that implementation's contract_version_id differs from named_contract_version_id; then each input port in port name order does not fit by fit_port_value, values read from their StoredValues and checked against the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant, each spooled file of a SpooledFilesRef taken by its SpooledFile facts, its media type equal to the port's and its size_bytes within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_TRIAL_FIXTURE_BYTES_MAX constant; every check comes before any byte is copied, so a refusal copies and writes nothing.

read_records: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST first raise StoreInternalError, before any record is looked up, when the query's arguments are malformed for its kind (a record_type that has no such identity form, an empty identity list or a field of another kind); then raise UnknownReferenceError naming the first missing record, in the order given for identity queries and in the order the relation's fields name them for a relation (an ElementKey names its run); a corpus digest is a value and is never missing, RunsByStatus and AttemptsByStatus name no record, and ActivationBeforeRun finding no activation raises StoreInternalError.

translate_failure: [FIELD_PROJECTION] Maps a failure to its code of = models.RefusalCode: UnknownReferenceError to unknown_reference, RefusedError to refused, InvalidRequestError and NonCanonicalValueError to invalid_request; StoreInternalError, StopRequiredError and every other exception to internal_error.
precedent.why: The later notes make missing referenced records propagate as unknown_reference, reserve refused for stated validation failures, and use internal_error only for malformed internal queries or broken invariants.

precedent.topic: Required port coverage in authored trial inputs and expected outputs
quotes: add_trial_case: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Raises UnknownReferenceError for an unknown contract version; then RefusedError naming the first name in inputs that is not an input port of the contract version, then the first name in expected_outputs that is not an output port, each taken by name; then checks each input port and, when expected_outputs is given, each output port, in port name order, by fit_port_value with the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant for value ports and the imported RELEASE_CEILING_TRIAL_FIXTURE_BYTES_MAX constant for file ports, a file candidate taking the payload's digest, size and the port's media type; the first failing check, presence, carriage, schema then size, raises RefusedError naming port and check, and nothing is written. A trial case therefore names exactly the contract's input ports, and expected_outputs is either absent or names exactly every output port: a partial expected_outputs, and an empty object, is given and fails presence at its first missing port; only absence means no expected outputs.
precedent.why: The later notes explicitly require exact input coverage and make expected outputs either absent or complete.

precedent.topic: startup manifest and capability validation scope
quotes: read_service_record: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Raises RefusedError naming the first failing check of the record itself, in this order: the record is absent at that revision, is not valid JSON, lacks service or capabilities, its service field differs from service_id, two capabilities share a name.

check_installed_instances: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Takes the services the installation holds a credential for, in service_id order by Unicode code point, and for each raises RefusedError naming that service at the first failure: first the credential header name equals a name in the imported KERNEL_SET_HEADER_NAMES constant compared without regard to case, host included, checked without reading the manifest; then, only when the installation selects an instance for the service, its record read by read_service_record fails any check, or the selected instance named in the record has a required header whose name equals the credential header name compared without regard to case.

check_installed_instances: [BEHAVIOR] A service with no selected instance, or whose record lists no instance of the selected name, fails nothing here; the check reads only the given installation and the manifest, never the store, and returns None when every service passes.
precedent.why: The later notes limit startup validation to credential-bearing services, ordered by service_id, and to top-level service-record checks plus the selected instance's credential-header collision.

precedent.topic: spool-ceiling refusal cleanup and state semantics
quotes: spool_file: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise RefusedError when the size of content exceeds the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SPOOL_FILE_BYTES_MAX constant, or when the run's spool, counted as the bytes of the files already in it, less a file no SpooledFile record names at this file's position, plus content, would exceed the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SPOOL_RUN_BYTES_MAX constant; on that refusal it removes this file and every file already spooled under the same run_id, producer_node_id, map_index and attempt_number, so nothing of that attempt's files is kept, while files of earlier attempts stay. The attempt_number of the key is the element's next number as the caller read it; spool_file does not assign one.

spool_file: [VALIDATION_ERROR] When removing this attempt's files on a ceiling refusal fails, MUST raise StoreInternalError instead of RefusedError, so a caller never reads a refusal as "nothing of the attempt is kept" while files of it remain; the files left stay unnamed in the run's spool, counted toward the spool ceiling, until remove_run_spool or a later write to their position.

spool_file: [RETURN_SHAPE] Returns FileFacts with the hexadecimal SHA-256 content_digest, size_bytes and the given media_type; it writes no SpooledFile record, which the caller's later record_change writes.
precedent.why: State 6 explicitly permits a ceiling refusal to remove files from earlier spool_file calls for the same attempt, converts cleanup failure to StoreInternalError with unnamed residual files, and defines the successful return value.
